recognize_zh: 高倍骨髓抹片中，箭頭指出的細胞比周圍成熟細胞大，核圓、染色質細緻，周邊有少量淡藍、帶小空泡的細胞質，屬於母細胞；其餘背景為成熟中的顆粒球與紅血球前驅細胞。
features: Arrowed cells are large blasts with round to oval nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli
Rim of pale to moderately basophilic cytoplasm with fine vacuolation in the arrowed cells
No Auer rods or distinct azurophilic granules in the arrowed blasts
Background of maturing granulocytes (myelocytes, metamyelocytes, band and segmented neutrophils) and erythroid precursors
Scattered small mature lymphocytes and normoblasts for size comparison
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear at high power shows a mixture of maturing granulocytic and erythroid elements. Interspersed are larger blasts (arrows) with round nuclei, finely dispersed chromatin, inconspicuous nucleoli and a rim of basophilic, finely vacuolated cytoplasm lacking granules or Auer rods. Morphology alone does not establish lineage, and the blast count requires a full differential. In a patient with a history of precursor B lymphoblastic leukemia, these blasts are suggestive of relapse, to be confirmed by flow cytometry.

ddx.vs: Hematogones are smaller with very scant cytoplasm and smudged homogeneous chromatin, and flow cytometry shows orderly maturation rather than an aberrant blast cluster.
Myeloblasts more often show azurophilic granules, Auer rods and MPO positivity, which are absent in lymphoblasts.
Promyelocytes have abundant cytoplasm with azurophilic granules and a paranuclear hof, whereas these blasts have scant agranular cytoplasm.
